clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests for deviation profiles; F-tests for idiosyncrasy; Spearman correlations of tract-wise profiles across groups; Unsupervised clustering (hierarchical/k-means) for group separation; Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) linking WM deviations and cognition.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: WM tract deviation and idiosyncrasy patterns are similar between early-stage schizophrenia and ASD/ADHD, with similarity diminishing in chronic schizophrenia.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Schizophrenia shows more negative deviation and greater idiosyncrasy than ASD/ADHD, especially in chronic stage; early-stage schizophrenia profiles correlate with ASD/ADHD. Unsupervised clustering cannot separate schizophrenia from ASD/ADHD using WM deviation features. CCA reveals shared brain–cognition covariation across disorders.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Propensity score matching for age used in subgroup comparisons (see STable 6).
